description: PRD-82A: Sequential Mission Coordinator — user says 'do this project' → coordinator decomposes into tasks → assigns roster agents → executes sequentially → verifies each output → human reviews. One task at a time. No contractors, no budget gates, no parallel dispatch.

userStories.title: Create MissionDispatcher with sequential execution
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the dispatcher that claims queued tasks, selects agents, and calls execute_with_prompt().
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/modules/coordination/dispatcher.py
Implement MissionDispatcher class
dispatch_next(db, run) method: find queued tasks via DependencyResolver.get_ready_tasks(), pick first by sequence_number
Sequential enforcement: if ANY task for this run is in state ASSIGNED or RUNNING, do NOT dispatch (return None)

Use optimistic claim pattern: UPDATE orchestration_tasks SET state='assigned', assigned_agent_id=:agent_id, version_id=version_id+1 WHERE id=:task_id AND state='queued' AND version_id=:expected — if 0 rows affected, skip (another instance claimed it)
Select agent via AgentMatcher.match() — if no match, transition task to failed with failure_reason_code='no_agent_available'
After successful claim, call AgentFactory.execute_with_prompt() with the task's description as prompt and assigned agent
On execute_with_prompt() completion: store output in task.output, transition to 'completed'
On execute_with_prompt() exception: transition to 'failed' with failure_reason_code='agent_error', store error in failure_detail
Create board task for the orchestration task via board bridge before dispatch
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: CRITICAL: The dispatch claim pattern (PRD-82A Section 4.4) prevents double-dispatch. Use raw SQL via db.execute(text(...)) for the atomic UPDATE since SQLAlchemy ORM version_id_col doesn't support the conditional UPDATE pattern directly. After claim succeeds, load the task fresh for the ORM. execute_with_prompt() is in agent_factory.py — check its current signature.

Stall detection: RUNNING task with no state change for 300s → transition to 'stalled', set failure_reason_code='agent_timeout'

The 60s/300s thresholds should come from config.py — add COORDINATOR_ASSIGNED_STALL_THRESHOLD_SECONDS and COORDINATOR_RUNNING_STALL_THRESHOLD_SECONDS.

userStories.title: Create DeterministicChecker for verification
userStories.description: As a developer, I need deterministic checks that validate task output before burning an LLM verification call.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/modules/coordination/deterministic_checks.py
Implement DeterministicChecker class
check(output, criteria) method — criteria is a list of check dicts from task.verification_criteria
Support 8 check types: format_regex, min_length, max_length, required_sections, json_schema, url_valid, contains_keywords, word_count_range
format_regex: output matches the provided regex pattern
min_length / max_length: character count bounds
required_sections: output contains all listed markdown section headers (e.g., '## Summary')
json_schema: if output is JSON, validate against provided schema
url_valid: any URLs in output are well-formed
contains_keywords: output contains all listed keywords
word_count_range: word count within [min, max] bounds
Returns DeterministicResult(passed: bool, failures: list[str]) — failures list describes which checks failed and why
If any check with must_pass=True fails, short-circuit and return immediately
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Each criterion dict: {'type': 'min_length', 'value': 100, 'must_pass': True}. The must_pass flag means failure is instant FAIL — no LLM judge needed. Non-must_pass failures are informational and passed to the LLM judge for consideration. Use re module for regex, json module for schema validation.

userStories.title: Create VerificationService with cross-model LLM judge

acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/modules/coordination/verification.py
Implement VerificationService class
verify_task(db, task) method returns VerificationResult(verdict: str, scores: dict, reasoning: str) where verdict is 'pass', 'fail', or 'partial'
Step 1: Run DeterministicChecker — if must_pass check fails, return verdict='fail' immediately
Step 2: Select verifier model — if task agent used Claude family, use GPT-4o; if GPT family, use Claude. Use config for model names (not hardcoded)
Step 3: LLM judge call with prompt: task description + expected output criteria + actual output + deterministic check results → structured verdict
LLM judge scores: relevance (0-1), completeness (0-1), accuracy (0-1), format_compliance (0-1)
verdict='pass' if all scores >= 0.7, 'fail' if any score < 0.4, 'partial' otherwise
Store verification result as OrchestrationEvent with event_type='verification_completed' and scores in payload
Handle LLM judge errors: up to 2 retries on the verification call itself
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Cross-model verification is a core PRD-82A principle (Section 5, principle 4). The model family detection: check if the agent's model string contains 'claude' or 'gpt' or 'deepseek' etc. Use config.VERIFICATION_MODEL_MAPPING or similar to define the cross-model pairs. The LLM call goes through OpenRouter like other LLM calls in the system.

On verdict='pass': transition task to 'verified', sync board status to 'done'
On verdict='fail': if attempt_number < max_retries, transition to 'retrying' with failure_reason_code='verification_fail', inject verifier reasoning into task context for retry
On verdict='fail' with attempt_number >= max_retries: transition to 'failed' with failure_reason_code='max_retries_exhausted'

Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The verification flow: completed → verifying → verified (or retrying/failed). When retrying, the verifier's reasoning gets injected into the task's input_context so the agent sees what went wrong. Token tracking: add verification tokens to task.tokens_used and run.tokens_used.

userStories.description: As a developer, I need the REST API endpoints for creating and managing missions.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/api/missions.py with FastAPI APIRouter
POST /api/missions — accepts {goal: str, config: dict optional}, calls CoordinatorService.create_mission(), returns 201 with run_id
GET /api/missions — list missions for workspace, paginated (limit/offset), filterable by state query param
GET /api/missions/{id} — returns full mission detail: run + tasks (with states) + recent events
POST /api/missions/{id}/approve — calls approve_plan(), accepts optional {modifications: dict}
POST /api/missions/{id}/reject — calls reject_plan(), requires {reason: str}
POST /api/missions/{id}/review — calls review_mission(), accepts {verdict: 'accept'|'reject', task_feedback: dict optional}
POST /api/missions/{id}/pause — calls pause_mission()
POST /api/missions/{id}/resume — calls resume_mission()
POST /api/missions/{id}/cancel — calls cancel_mission()
All endpoints require auth (use existing auth dependency from other API routers)
All endpoints enforce workspace isolation (workspace_id from auth context)
Pydantic request/response models for all endpoints
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Follow the pattern of existing API routers (check orchestrator/api/ for examples like board.py or agents.py). Use the existing auth dependency that extracts workspace_id from the Clerk token. Response models should use 'mission' terminology per PRD-82A Section 10 (API uses 'mission', DB uses 'orchestration'). The GET detail endpoint should include output_summary if available.

userStories.title: Mount missions router in main app
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the missions API router registered in the FastAPI application.
acceptanceCriteria: Find the main FastAPI app setup (likely orchestrator/main.py or orchestrator/api/__init__.py)
Import the missions router from orchestrator/api/missions.py
Mount it with app.include_router(missions_router) with appropriate prefix and tags
Verify the endpoints appear in /docs (OpenAPI schema)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Simple registration. Check how other routers are mounted — match the pattern (prefix, tags, dependencies).
